html:
The Gaelic Athletic Association was founded on 1 November 1884 in Thurles, County Tipperary, to revive and organise Irish games, above all hurling and Gaelic football.

It was part of the Gaelic revival of the late 1800s, which also gave rise to the Gaelic League for the Irish language. It banned its members from playing English sports such as soccer and rugby, and barred British soldiers and police. Clubs were organised by parish and county, which gave them deep local roots.

Many leaders of the Easter Rising and the War of Independence came from its ranks. On Bloody Sunday in 1920 British forces fired on the crowd at a match in Croke Park, killing fourteen. The GAA, still amateur, remains the largest sports body in Ireland. Compare the English Football Association.
